question: What is the main job of the immune system?

options.A: Breaking down dietary proteins into amino acids
options.B: Pumping oxygenated blood to the body tissues
options.C: Filtering waste products from the blood
options.D: Recognizing self from non-self to defend against germs

explanation: The immune system protects the body by telling the difference between its own healthy cells and harmful foreign invaders. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T83#GNS214_U1_T83_h1)

question: Which part of the body is primarily responsible for producing white blood cells?
explanation: White blood cells are produced and mature inside the soft, spongy tissue found in the center of bones, known as bone marrow. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T83#GNS214_U1_T83_h1)

question: How does innate immunity differ from adaptive immunity?

options.A: Innate immunity targets only viruses, while adaptive immunity targets bacteria
options.B: Innate immunity requires previous exposure, while adaptive immunity works at birth
options.C: Innate immunity relies only on antibodies, while adaptive immunity uses physical barriers
options.D: Innate immunity provides fast, general defense, while adaptive immunity is specific and builds memory

explanation: Innate defenses are present from birth and react the same way to all germs, whereas adaptive defenses target specific invaders and remember them for the future. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T83#GNS214_U1_T83_h2)

question: Stomach acid and unbroken skin belong to which type of immune defense?
explanation: Physical barriers like skin and chemical barriers like stomach acid form part of the non-specific innate immune system that everyone is born with. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T83#GNS214_U1_T83_h2)

question: Why is passive immunity only temporary?

options.A: Antibodies multiply too fast and overwhelm the lymphatic system
options.B: Maternal antibodies destroy the bone marrow
options.C: The body does not produce its own antibodies or memory cells
options.D: Passive antibodies are quickly converted into energy by the liver

explanation: Passive immunity simply provides ready-made antibodies without teaching the body to make its own, so protection fades as those antibodies break down. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T83#GNS214_U1_T83_h3)

question: An infant receiving protective antibodies through breast milk is an example of what?
explanation: Breast milk naturally passes antibodies from mother to baby, offering temporary protection without the baby's immune system producing them. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T83#GNS214_U1_T83_h3)

question: Receiving a vaccine to trigger antibody production is an example of what?
explanation: Vaccines introduce safe antigens into the body, prompting the immune system to actively create its own antibodies and memory cells. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T83#GNS214_U1_T83_h4)

question: What type of immunity do you get after recovering from a natural measles infection?
explanation: Surviving a real infection exposes the body to the pathogen, sparking an active immune response and long-lasting protection. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T83#GNS214_U1_T83_h4)

question: Which specific white blood cells are responsible for making antibodies?
explanation: B-lymphocytes turn into plasma cells, which act as antibody factories during an immune response. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T83#GNS214_U1_T83_h5)

question: What is the main role of an antibody when it binds to an antigen?

options.A: To supply nutrients to surrounding tissues
options.B: To copy the genetic material of the germ
options.C: To transport oxygen away from the infected site
options.D: To neutralize the invader or mark it for destruction

explanation: Antibodies lock onto specific antigens to stop them from causing harm and to flag them so other immune cells can destroy them easily. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T83#GNS214_U1_T83_h5)

question: How does herd immunity protect vulnerable people who cannot take vaccines?

options.A: By reducing the number of susceptible people so the disease cannot easily spread
options.B: By destroying all bacteria in a specific area
options.C: By turning active immunity into passive immunity in the community
options.D: By strengthening the skin barrier of newborns automatically

explanation: When most people in a community are immune, the germ struggles to find new hosts, which stops transmission and protects unvaccinated individuals. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T83#GNS214_U1_T83_h6)

question: What factor mainly determines the herd immunity threshold needed for a disease?

options.A: The average daily temperature of the local climate
options.B: The number of available hospitals in the country
options.C: The total landmass of the region
options.D: How contagious the infectious disease is

explanation: Diseases that spread very easily require a much higher percentage of immune people in the population to halt transmission. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T83#GNS214_U1_T83_h6)

question: What is the term for the gradual weakening of immune function in older adults?
explanation: Immunosenescence describes the natural decline in immune system efficiency that happens as people age. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T83#GNS214_U1_T83_h7)

question: Which factor is NOT typically linked to a weakened immune response?

options.C: Chronic stress causing high cortisol levels

explanation: Good nutrition supports overall immune health, whereas malnutrition, chronic stress, and poorly controlled diabetes can all weaken immunity. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T83#GNS214_U1_T83_h7)
